parameters.name: Attributes Class
parameters.description: Attribute class to analyze: Point, Vertex, or Primitive.

parameters.name: Group
parameters.description: If there are input groups, specifying a group name will restrict analysis to that group.

parameters.name: Number of Elements in Group
parameters.description: Output an attribute with the number of elements in the selected group.

parameters.name: Input Attributes
parameters.description: Input attributes to analyze. Use * for all attributes.

parameters.name: Append Attrib Names to Output
parameters.description: Include input attribute names in output attribute names for clarity.

parameters.name: Combine Components
parameters.description: Combine all components of a vector attribute into one value before analysis.

parameters.name: Centroid
parameters.description: Output average of min and max values.

parameters.name: Index of Minimum
parameters.description: Output point index with minimum value.

parameters.name: Index of Maximum
parameters.description: Output point index with maximum value.

parameters.name: Num Points/Vertices/Primitives
parameters.description: Output counts of points, vertices, and primitives.

parameters.name: Dimension
parameters.description: Output dimension sizes of this POP.

parameters.name: P Attribute Values
parameters.description: Choose which analyzed result to place in the P attribute.

useCases: Get statistical summary of point cloud attributes (min, max, average, sum)
Compute bounding box from position data (Min/Max of P)
Find the point with extreme values using Index of Minimum/Maximum
Normalize attribute values based on min/max analysis
Reduce vectors to scalar using Combine Components before analysis
examples: Analyze POP (Average=On, P=Input Attribute Average) → outputs centroid as P
Analyze POP (Min=On, Max=On, Size=On on P) → outputs bounding box dimensions
Analyze POP (Combine Components=Add on Cd) → sum RGB to single luminance value

commonCombinations.description: Filter points based on statistical analysis of their attributes
Normalize attribute values based on min/max analysis
Feed analysis results back into the GPU pipeline
Export analysis results to CHOPs for parameter control

troubleshooting: Results are a single point on GPU — stay on GPU for best performance
For multi-attribute analysis, use * or separate Analyze POPs per attribute
Per-component analysis: for vector P, Min(0)=min X, Min(1)=min Y, etc.
Use POP to CHOP for CPU access (one frame delayed) or pass point as input to other POPs
description: Analyzes any point, vertex or primitive attributes of a POP and outputs a single point containing resulting statistics. Computes average, min, max, sum, size, index, centroid, RMS power, and more. Per-component analysis for vectors (e.g., Min(0) = min X). Supports Combine Components to reduce vectors to scalar before analysis.
